title: spec.json — requirements baseline (written once by the Planner)

mode.description: Build mode. 'greenfield' (default when absent) = a new app scaffolded from scratch. 'extend' = new functionality added to a pre-existing app; the extend-Planner sets this and populates baseline_check.

baseline_check.description: EXTEND-mode regression gate: how to confirm existing behavior still works after each new build. Absent on greenfield specs. The Generator re-runs it after building and the Evaluator re-runs it at verdict; a broken baseline fails the requirement even if the new criteria pass.

command.description: Shell command proving existing behavior (e.g. 'pytest', 'npm test', an exit-0 scorecard). null if the app has no runnable check — Evaluator falls back to a smoke test.

complexity.description: Verification ceremony tier. trivial → fast-path (self-contract + build); standard → propose + auto-accept + build; complex → full adversarial negotiation. Absent/unknown defaults to complex.

verification.description: How pass/fail is decided. command → run a process and assert its exit code / stdout (a CLI/backend capability; no browser — the contract's test_steps ARE shell commands with expected exit/output). deterministic → read from data-*/DOM/computed CSS in a browser. visual → needs screenshot judgment. command and deterministic are mechanical and can use a cheaper verdict model; visual needs the heavier one. Absent/unknown defaults to visual.

extends.description: Optional id of an earlier requirement this one generalizes/narrows and likely satisfies with no new code. Triggers a verify-first probe (verdict against existing code before spending a build). Omit for genuinely-new requirements.

examples.app: Notes — a minimal single-user notes web app

requirements.description: User can create a note; it appears in the notes list without a full page reload.

requirements.rationale: A notes app that forgets is useless.
